verdicts.quote: a user finds "Grok Bot" in App Launcher, opens the app, and lands on the chat page whose URL path is `/lightning/n/<TabApiName>` ... Out of scope: Experience Cloud, Salesforce mobile app specifics, utility-bar or record-page embedding.
Nothing in the product reads Salesforce records on the user's behalf (A-4), so there is no sharing/CRUD/FLS exposure ... sharing: n/a (no record access)
Nothing in the product reads Salesforce records on the user's behalf (A-4) ... object CRUD: n/a; FLS: n/a; configuration read is by trusted system code
one permission set (name per AD-6) is the only way to (a) see the chat app/tab, (b) call the product's server methods, (c) use the xAI credential principal.
verdicts.missing: Who may administer (edit config, enter key, assign the permission set) is only 'org admin', with no permission set or named permission; G-6 leaves 'who may assign the permission set' open.

verdicts.quote: Who may read: only the person at that browser. No other user, admin or process can read it from the org by design.
the call is synchronous inside the user's request; there is no background job, queue or webhook. ... no callout after uncommitted work (product has no DML).
verdicts.missing: The spec addresses the no-callout-after-DML rule but chooses a synchronous callout; no asynchronous (Queueable/future/batch) design is stated.

verdicts.quote: the key is stored only in the org's external-credential facility, entered by an admin after deploy. It never appears in source files, repository history, configuration records, Apex or LWC code, test fixtures, run notes, logs
Apex limits ... <=100 callouts/transaction (this product uses 1), <=120 s cumulative (default timeout 60 s leaves headroom), no callout after uncommitted work
verdicts.missing: Heap size and CPU time limits are not named or given numbers.

verdicts.quote: Apex callout code isolated in one service class with the callout mockable; all Apex tests use `HttpCalloutMock`, none hit the network (no `seeAllData`).
a Named Credential references it as the callout endpoint (`callout:<NamedCredential>/v1/...`)
Server → Credential → xAI: HTTPS call (synchronous). ... UI: if its request token is still current, append bot message, clear Pending (T-2) else discard (T-5).
verdicts.missing: The reply is assumed to return inline from the Apex call; no platform event, CDC, polled status or LMS notification mechanism is specified.

verdicts.quote: pressing Retry re-sends the same text, and on success shows exactly one user bubble and one bot bubble for it (no duplicate).
there is no background job, queue or webhook.
verdicts.missing: Concurrent-request limits (e.g. org-wide concurrent long-running request limit) and what a user sees when a request cannot be accepted are not stated.

verdicts.quote: Other HTTP 4xx ... `REQUEST_REJECTED` ... HTTP 5xx | `UPSTREAM_ERROR` | Grok is having trouble; try again | Callout timeout ... `TIMEOUT` | Grok did not answer in time
HTTP 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Grok is busy or the key's limit is reached; try again shortly ... the product does not retry automatically.
Callout timeout ... `TIMEOUT` | Grok did not answer in time | 2xx but no assistant text parseable | `BAD_RESPONSE`
verdicts.missing: A truncated reply (e.g. length/stop-reason cut-off) that still parses is not addressed; what the user sees for a partial answer is undecided.

verdicts.quote: the transcript exists only in the open page's memory (AD-4) ... Nothing is written to org records, files, cache or logs.
verdicts.missing: No record shape is defined; model identifier and token/usage counts are not captured anywhere.

verdicts.quote: lifetime = until New chat, page reload, or navigating away from the page. Nothing is written to org records, files, cache or logs.
v1 sends Grok only what the user typed (plus admin-configured instructions and earlier turns of the same chat). It does **not** read or send Salesforce records.
each request carries the system prompt plus the most recent messages ... trimmed from the oldest end until the count is <= the window (default 20 non-system messages)
A message that is empty after trimming, or longer than the configured maximum (default 4,000 characters ...), is rejected ... Boundary: 4,000 characters accepted; 4,001 rejected.
an org admin can change, in Setup and without a code deploy: the Grok model ID, the system prompt, the callout timeout
verdicts.missing: No off switch is specified, and operator visibility of failed requests is left open (G-10: 'default: the product writes no log lines').

verdicts.quote: Owned event coverage: no audit trail of conversations (A-5).
verdicts.missing: No audit record of who asked what and what was answered, and no retention for one; the spec declines it.

verdicts.quote: Apex coverage target: 75% org-wide is the platform deploy gate for production; for a development org the gate may not apply
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credential differ per environment is not stated; production is out of scope.

verdicts.quote: the user sees a result (reply or error) no later than the configured callout timeout plus platform overhead ... the UI shows "thinking" only while a request is truly in flight
designed empty (welcome text, notice from R-9, suggested nothing-to-send state), loading (thinking indicator, disabled Send, `aria-busy`/live region), error (code-specific message with Retry)
Org records (any object) | any | **out of scope**, never read or written | unchanged ... redeploy preserves unrelated org state
